title: Cross-excursion usable-loss coupling cuts the run-type budget below θ on E_run(10^6)
statement: Exact Juggler dynamics prevent successive CycleMin-scale odd-run blocks from both realizing near-maximal usable floor loss, and the resulting two-excursion tax empties a leftover in E_run(10^6), in particular L=25781 or L=55293.
counterexamples: OOE-legal n=1000301 has U0=0.9737 and next-run U1=0.9945 at v1=5625317. max(U0+U1)=1.968, so consecutive excursion maxima equal the independent pair of maxima
OOOE-legal n=1018335 has min(U0,U1)=0.9767 with next OE at v1=13750405517 and U1=0.9846
On 1210 CycleMin-scale OOE pairs, P(U1>0.9|U0>0.9)=0.175 exceeds P(U>0.9)=0.066. Near-top losses are positively persistent. Finance-weighted correlation is ~0
A uniform factor 0.977 would bookkeeping-kill L=55293 and would not touch L=25781. That window maximum is not a CycleMin theorem
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / cross-excursion floor loss
notes: One-step remainders and consecutive-letter corners were already unrestricted. The multi-step signature is the same cell-top logarithm along two Q-blocks. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: CycleMin-scale pairs from odds in [10^6+1, 10^6+20001) and [oe_start_min(10^6+1), oe_start+8000); 99 run-type survivors; spotlights L=25781 and 55293
